chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a mosque that is inside a house, so the people of the house intend to widen a section of it or relocate it to another place. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about a place that is filthy, then is cleaned and made into a mosque. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Soil is poured upon it until it covers it, so it becomes purer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expanding or moving a mosque inside a house, and how is impurity removed from a spot designated as a mosque?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of domestic worship spaces, permitting the expansion or relocation of a mosque within a private home, which reflects the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of the home as a microcosm of the mosque. Additionally, it establishes a specific purification method for converting impure ground into a prayer area by covering it with soil, ensuring ritual purity for prostration. This ruling underscores the practical adaptability of fiqh in domestic settings while maintaining strict standards of taharah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the Masjid which happens to be inside the house, so the people of the household intend to widen the range of it or relocate it to another place. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the place which happens to be filthy, then is cleaned up and made into a Masjid. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The soil would be poured upon it until it is covered, so it would be clean’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Aban ‘Uthman from abu al-Jarud who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a Masjid which is in a house and the people of the house want to expand it to a certain extent or relocate it in another place. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’

He (the narrator) has said that he then asked him (the Imam) about a place which is filthy, then it is cleansed and is made a Masjid. He (the Imam) said, ‘Soil is poured on it until it is covered; it is cleaner.’”
